evidence.curator_note: Charge-site-initiated (inductive, 'i') cleavage of the protonated ephedrine [M+H]+ (m/z 166) drawn in Eq. 4.29: C6H5-CHOH-CHCH3-N(+)H2CH3 -> C6H5-CHOH-(+)CHCH3 + H2N-CH3. Book draws 1 arc; move <1> is drawn -- a single full (double-barbed, two-electron) curved arrow from the C9-N11 sigma bond onto N11. No implicit homolysis hook is required: inductive cleavage is heterolytic, so this one two-electron arrow fully balances the flow -- the C-N bonding pair becomes an N lone pair (N+ -> neutral CH3NH2) and the carbon C9 that loses the bond becomes the m/z 135 carbocation. The C9 cation the book draws is the localized secondary cation (stabilized by the beta-hydroxyl / homoconjugation, not itself benzylic); Kekule/aromatic form of the intact phenyl ring is retained unchanged.

rule_index.json cross-links equation 4.29 to the single MØD rule IMS_4_29 (DFS: ...[C]7([H]8)[O]9([H]10)[C]11([H]12)[C]13([H]14)([H]15)([H]16)[N+]17([H]18)([H]19)[C]20... >> ...[C+]11...[C]13... . [N]17...[C]20...). VERIFIED MISMATCH, not support: (1) the DFS linearization bonds N17 to the CH3 carbon C13 (H14-H16), making C13 pentavalent (C11, N17, 3 H) -- MOD tolerates this graph but it is not ephedrine; (2) the cleaved bond is C13-N17, yet the new (+) is placed on C11, so the broken bond is NOT incident to the charge-bearing atom (same class of geometry defect as IMS_4_11/4_9); the book instead cleaves the C-N bond and puts the (+) on that very carbon; (3) O9 is written as an ether bridge (two C-neighbors, C7 and C11) rather than ephedrine's terminal hydroxyl (one C-neighbor), so the LHS cannot subgraph-match real ephedrine at the oxygen. The reaction TYPE (heterolytic C-N inductive cleavage -> carbocation + CH3NH2 loss) is correct, but IMS_4_29 does not reproduce this substrate. Listed in rule_mismatches.

This is a chemical-ionization (CH4 reagent) reaction, not EI: the precursor is the even-electron protonated molecule [M+H]+ (m/z 166, labeled '166 MH+' in the lower CI panel), so the precursor is charge +1 / radical 0 (NOT [M]+.); ms_context is set to CI accordingly (deviating from the EI template to stay faithful to the figure). The m/z 135 fragment is labeled in the CI spectrum and named in the surrounding text ('the small peak produced in the CI spectrum at m/z 135'); it is a small, genuinely observed peak but no numeric intensity is printed, so relative_intensity is omitted. observed_mz 135.0804 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of C9H11O+ (electron-mass corrected); the book prints only the nominal integer 135.
